newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH BONDS END OFF, TRACKING WEAKER BUNDS.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH BONDS END OFF, TRACKING WEAKER BUNDS.

text.p: Markka bonds ended lower on
Wednesday, tracking weakness in Europe where bond markets
remained beset by jitters over the final round of the French
elections to be held on Sunday, dealers said.
"The market has weakened along with Germany. The French
elections have caused uncertainty," one dealer said, noting
however that the long-end spread over Germany was stable at
35-36 basis points.
"This negative sentiment will probably continue," said
another dealer who, nevertheless, saw an opportunity at these
levels for a well-bid auction of the 2006 bond on Thursday.
The markka traded in a tight range against the German mark,
with interest on both sides, forex dealers said.
DEM/FIM was seen staying within a range of 3.01 to 3.025,
dealers said.
Some jitters were caused by uncertainty in Sweden where the
market waited for a clear signal from the government on whether
Sweden would join, or stay out of, the third phase of European
economic and monetary union, dealers said.
A sharp weakening or strengthening of the Swedish crown
could have repercussions for the markka, one dealer said.
